grade.stack_chosen: TypeScript/Node with a BullMQ queue on the existing Redis and a separate worker process; finished PDFs cached in Redis for an hour
grade.notes: It made the right architectural move: rendering goes through a BullMQ queue on the Redis they already run, into a separate TS worker meant to run as its own Fly process group, with no language switch. It never does the 3,000 × 0.4 s ≈ 20 CPU-minutes maths and doesn't suggest pre-generating reports. It also has gaps: base64 PDFs in Redis with a one-hour expiry instead of object storage with signed URLs, a 25 s wait inside the HTTP request, no queue-depth monitoring, and no explicit advice to stay in TypeScript.
